full_judgment: 3. The government as defendant No.1 con-tested the said suit by filing written statement, contending, inter alia, that during the District Settlement Survey the suit land was recorded as Zamindarts Hat-Bazar. After the enactment of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 due to abolishing of Zamindari system the suit land had been vested to the government and during the M.R.R. survey the suit land was correctly recorded in the name of government in Khas Khatian No.1. The plaintiffs predecessor and thereafter the plaintiff took lease of the suit land for the years from 1365 to 1376 B.S., from 1379 to 1385 B.S. and from 1373 to 1392 B.S. admitting the suit land as government property. The plaintiff as well as his predecessor had no right, title and possession in the suit land. Abdul Mannan along with others numbering eighteen had been doing business in the land of plots No.2105 and 2106 after taking yearly lease from the government. The suit is barred by limitation. Since the government has right, title and possession in the suit land the plaintiff is not entitled to get relief as prayed for.
